narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story; calm and unhurried.

joseph-the-patriarch.name: Joseph
joseph-the-patriarch.note: Ruler of Egypt under Pharao; capable, tender toward his father and forgiving toward his brothers.

pharaoh.name: Pharao
pharaoh.note: King of Egypt; gracious and generous toward Joseph's family.

josephs-brothers.name: Joseph's brothers
josephs-brothers.note: The sons of Jacob speaking together; deferential before Pharao, fearful and penitent before Joseph.

chanaanites.name: Inhabitants of Chanaan
chanaanites.note: Onlookers remarking on the Egyptians' great mourning at Atad.

1.t: And when Joseph saw this, he fell upon his father's face, weeping and kissing him.

2.t: And he commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father.

3.t: And while they were fulfilling his commands, there passed forty days: for this was the manner with bodies that were embalmed, and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.

4.t: And the time of the mourning being expired, Joseph spoke to the family of Pharao:
If I have found favour in your sight, speak in the ears of Pharao:

5.t: For my father made me swear to him, saying: Behold I die; thou shalt bury me in my sepulchre which I have digged for myself in the land of Chanaan. So I will go up and bury my father, and return.

6.t: Go up and bury thy father according as he made thee swear.

7.t: So he went up, and there went with him all the ancients of Pharao's house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt.

8.t: And the house of Joseph with his brethren, except their children, and their flocks and herds, which they left in the land of Gessen.

9.t: He had also in his train chariots and horsemen: and it was a great company.

10.t: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is situated beyond the Jordan: where celebrating the exequies with a great and vehement lamentation, they spent full seven days.

11.t: And when the inhabitants of Chanaan saw this, they said:
This is a great mourning to the Egyptians.
And therefore the name of that place was called, The mourning of Egypt.

12.t: So the sons of Jacob did as he had commanded them.

13.t: And carrying him into the land of Chanaan, they buried him in the double cave, which Abraham had bought together with the field for a possession of a burying place, of Ehpron, the Hethite, over against Mambre.

14.t: And Joseph returned into Egypt with his brethren, and all that were in his company, after he had buried his father.

15.t: Now he being dead, his brethren were afraid, and talked one with another:
Lest perhaps he should remember the wrong he suffered, and requite us all the evil that we did to him.

16.t: And they sent a message to him, saying:
Thy father commanded us before he died,
16.q: a message sent to Joseph (perhaps by a messenger); given to the brothers whose words it is

17.t: That we should say thus much to thee from him: I beseech thee to forget the wickedness of thy brethren, and the sin and malice they practised against thee: we also pray thee, to forgive the servants of the God of thy father this wickedness.
17.q: continuation of the sent message, including the words attributed to Jacob

17.t: And when Joseph heard this, he wept.

18.t: And his brethren came to him; and worshipping prostrate on the ground, they said:

19.t: Fear not: can we resist the will of God?

20.t: You thought evil against me: but God turned it into good, that he might exalt me, as at present you see, and might save many people.

21.t: Fear not: I will feed you and your children.
And he comforted them, and spoke gently and mildly.

22.t: And he dwelt in Egypt with all his father's house; and lived a hundred and ten years. And he saw the children of Ephraim to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the sons of Manasses, were born on Joseph's knees.

23.t: After which he told his brethren:
God will visit you after my death, and will make you go up out of this land, to the land which he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

24.t: And he made them swear to him, saying:
God will visit you, carry my bones with you out of this place:

25.t: And he died, being a hundred and ten years old. And being embalmed, he was laid in a coffin in Egypt.
